feature.title: Hub regressions vs acceptance benchmarks
feature.request: if you look at the last session, youll as we were implementing the hub plan, we've had some regressions for some of the visualizations.  Let's take a hard look at every metric that is not being met by acceptance criteria based on what is currently in origin main, and divulge possible solutions that will help us meet our benchmarks for all files in ./debug-in.

problem.statement: Since the audio hub (PR 95) and the dancer hub-bass commits, some visualizers react worse than before and several acceptance criteria from the audio-engine-alignment and rhythm-stability-followups plans are failing or unmeasured on the .debug-in tracks. Nobody has a current per-track, per-metric scorecard, so fixes are tuned against single tracks and break others.
users: Trevor, the developer tuning visualizers against .debug-in
Viewers watching hub-fed visualizers (dancing character, cubes and others) react to music
evidence: Gate timing regressed: imyourgirl 0.3 s to 2.8-3.0 s, summer2000 3.5 s to 4.0-7.9 s (rhythm-stability-results.md:33-35)
Cubes threshold crossings fell from about 30 to 17 of 61 beats after hub migration while the migration check passed (audio-presentation-audit.md:66-78)
Onset F below 0.9: no-kick-124 bass 0.67, bassline-kick-120 kick 0.76 (audio-alignment-findings.md:136-141)
Gate within 4 s fails on lonley 8.0 s and syncopationbass 16.8-17.9 s; clip spread p95 0.199 to 0.53 against 0.05
Hub bands are normalized to a running peak (hubConfig.ts:12-20) while bassGateConfig thresholds were tuned on raw BassPulse RMS
Six .debug-in tracks have no .beats.json; 2026-11-16/17 telemetry in .debug-out was never summarized

goals: Produce a repeatable scorecard of every applicable acceptance metric, for every .debug-in file and every hub-fed visualizer, on the current branch, with a pre-hub reference column
Identify the cause of each failing or regressed cell, by measurement
Bring every cell to at least its floor (absolute AC target and no worse than pre-hub) without dropping any other cell, and push reaction cells toward stretch targets above pre-hub
Make the scorecard a re-runnable no-regression check for later hub work (local, since .debug-in is uncommitted)
non_goals: Upgrading three.js or changing the rhythm tracker architecture beyond what a measured cause requires
Capture-delay work that needs loopback hardware
success_metrics: Floor: 100 percent of applicable cells pass their floor (absolute AC target and no worse than the pre-hub reference), excluding only cells deferred with user sign-off
Zero blocking cells that pass at the latest merged baseline fail after any slice

Stretch, cubes and each hub-fed reaction: at least 90 percent of labelled beats hit within 50 ms with false fires at most 10 percent of fires, on every kick track (pre-hub was about 30 of 61 crossings on drums-128)
Stretch, dancer gate: engages within 2 s of track start on every kick track (floor 4 s and pre-hub 0.3 s and 3.5 s on imyourgirl and summer2000)
Stretch, reaction latency: at most 30 ms plus one frame on every visualizer
constraints: No allocation per frame; logic outside React; reuse hub, useRhythm, useAnalyser (AGENTS.md rules)
format:check, lint, typecheck, test:coverage at 95 percent, build and test:e2e pass; bundle within .size-limit.json
Rhythm changes need live checks on all real tracks (rhythm-stability-results.md:254)
Telemetry stays in git-ignored .debug-out; .debug-in audio is not committed

decisions.question: Which code is the baseline measured on?
decisions.answer: The current branch feat/s8-dancing-character-hub-bass only (it contains origin/main plus 3 dancer-hub commits)

decisions.question: Which visualizers are in scope?
decisions.answer: Every visualizer that reads signals from the audio hub, plus cubes and trio-color-wave as reference controls

decisions.question: How do .debug-in tracks without .beats.json count?
decisions.answer: Tap ground truth first: a slice produces .beats.json for every .debug-in track that lacks one so every metric applies to every file

decisions.question: What wins when fixes conflict?
decisions.answer: Hit every AC with no trade-offs: a fix is accepted only if no track or metric drops below target

decisions.question: Beat error target for tapped real tracks
decisions.answer: At most 40 ms median, since tap jitter makes the 20 ms synthetic target unfair
decisions.rationale: User confirmed 40 ms median in round 2

decisions.question: Is the framing (problem, goals, non-goals, AC1-AC12) right?
Measure a pre-hub reference?
decisions.answer: Yes: run the same scorecard once on the commit before the hub merge (b449f56 first parent) in a worktree as a reference column; the current branch stays the baseline
decisions.rationale: Round 3; doc numbers came from a different harness

decisions.question: Are pre-hub values the goal?
decisions.answer: No: pre-hub is the floor and stretch targets are set above it where better is possible
decisions.rationale: Round 3: 30 of 61 beats is still many misses

decisions.question: Stretch target numbers
decisions.answer: 90 percent beat hit share at 50 ms with at most 10 percent false fires; gate within 2 s; latency at most 30 ms plus a frame; confirmed or adjusted at the S3 review
decisions.rationale: Hit share and false-fire bound are the planner's; 30 ms comes from the hub plan click target; user to confirm

decisions.question: Failures that predate the hub
decisions.answer: Own slices (gate rule, clip phase, tempo); if a fix needs a gate or tracker redesign the cell is deferred to a separate plan with user sign-off at review and excluded from the 100 percent

decisions.question: Keep AC10 migration?
decisions.answer: Keep as a late slice, gated on a before and after reaction cell per visualizer; bass-ink moves only onto the gate input S4 proves

decisions.question: Do live cells block merges?
decisions.answer: No: offline cells block; live cells are advisory, pass at 3 of 4 runs, and regress only when the median worsens beyond the S3 run-to-run spread

decisions.question: Which metrics apply to which tracks?
decisions.answer: Applicability matrix by class: onset F only on tracks with labelled onsets (synthetic); beat error and hit share n/a on beatless; drifting-tempo uses local bpm
decisions.rationale: onsetSweepRunner.ts:23-33 scores F only on labelled synthetic tracks (critic F2)

options.summary: Add one scorecard script that wraps the existing eval, sweep and debug tools into a committed pass/fail table, then fix only the measured failing cells, starting by retuning bassGateConfig thresholds to the hub's peak-normalized bass.
approach: Tap .beats.json for the six missing tracks with tap:beats (beatless gets an explicit no-beat truth) so every metric applies to every file (AC2).

Write scripts/scorecard.ts that shells out to eval:rhythm --alignment, sweep:onsets, debug:viz (cubes, trio-color-wave, dancing-character and each hub-fed visualizer) and debug:repeat, 4 runs per track, and parses their existing JSON/telemetry output.
Emit docs/scorecard.md (metric x track x visualizer: target, measured, pass/fail, spread) plus scorecard.json; verdicts are thresholds applied to medians so reruns match (AC1).
Add a --compare baseline.json flag that exits nonzero if any previously passing cell fails (AC12).
Commit the baseline on the current branch, then fix only the failing cells, one slice each, rerunning the scorecard per slice.
First fix: scale bassGateConfig thresholds (or feed the gate raw BassPulse again) for the dancer's hub bass; check imyourgirl, summer2000, lonley, syncopationbass (AC6, AC7).
Second fix: retune the cubes hub bass threshold for 30 of 61 beats on drums-128 (AC8); defer AC9, AC10 and AC11 to follow-up slices once measured.

contracts: npm run scorecard [-- --compare docs/scorecard.baseline.json] exits 0 only if no baseline-passing cell fails
scorecard.json cell: { metric, track, visualizer, target, median, spread, pass }
package.json gains one script entry, scorecard
pros: Reuses every existing tool, with no app code changes for measurement
The scorecard doubles as the regression gate
Fixes are driven by measured failures, not guesses
cons: debug:viz needs a live browser, so the full run is slow and semi-manual
Threshold retuning may trade tracks against each other (D4 forbids this)
Onset F failures (AC5) and AC9 may need tracker changes that this option defers
risks: Live telemetry is noisy and verdicts may flap; median of 4 runs with a tolerance band mitigates this
Tapped truth quality limits the 40 ms target
Retuning to hub bass may not recover the 0.3 s and 3.5 s gate times

options.summary: Build a deterministic scorecard with a committed baseline and a no-regression diff gate, then fix causes at the hub boundary by adding an absolute-scale (non-peak-normalized) band output and moving every private band or onset path onto the hub.
approach: Scorecard runner scripts/scorecard/: drives eval:rhythm --alignment, sweep:onsets, debug:viz and debug:repeat per track x visualizer (hub-fed plus cubes and trio-color-wave), 4 runs each; emits scorecard.json (target, median, spread, verdict) and scorecard.md.
Determinism: verdict uses the median of 4 runs with a per-metric tolerance band, and fixed seeds, so reruns give identical pass or fail; the raw telemetry stays in .debug-out.
Baseline gate: committed scorecard.baseline.json; scorecard:diff fails if any previously passing cell fails (AC12) and prints the cell-level delta for each slice.
Tap ground truth for the six tracks via tap:beats plus calibration; beatless gets an explicit no-beat truth that asserts the tracker never locks.
Cause isolation by ablation: replay:gate on dancer telemetry comparing raw BassPulse against hub bass, to confirm the normalization-versus-threshold mismatch before changing code.

Hub change: add an absolute-scale band channel (fixed reference gain, no running-peak divide) next to the normalized one; the dancer gate and cubes crossings read the absolute one so bassGateConfig thresholds and cube thresholds keep their tuned meaning. Onsets get a per-band detector retune from sweep:onsets (no-kick bass, kick).
Migrate cubes bars, bass-ink and trio sheets to hub bands and hub.onsets, then delete private analysis (AC10); add an order-independence e2e for AC11; each fix is one slice, re-scored before merge.

contracts: Hub snapshot gains absolute bands (same band keys, fixed-gain scale); existing normalized fields unchanged.

New npm scripts scorecard and scorecard:diff (exit nonzero on regression).
pros: Fixes the likely root cause once at the boundary instead of retuning per visualizer
Measured causes before code; the diff gate enforces D4 and AC12 mechanically
cons: Largest effort; 4 runs times many tracks times visualizers is slow
Two band scales in the hub is added API surface
Touches hub behavior shared by every visualizer

options.summary: Stop tuning each visualizer against live browser runs: make the hub emit a fixed-reference (absolute) band so thresholds tuned on raw RMS still hold, and make the scorecard an offline, deterministic replay of hub plus gate over the WAVs, committed as a ratchet baseline.
approach: Break the assumption that hub bands must be running-peak normalized for everyone: add a fixed-gain absolute channel (hub.abs.bass, calibrated to match BassPulse raw RMS scale) next to the normalized one; the dancer and cubes read it for gating, so bassGateConfig and pre-hub cube thresholds apply unchanged.

Break the assumption that scoring needs a live browser: build scripts/scorecard/ which decodes each WAV, drives the real hub, bassGate and cube trigger code headlessly through the existing replay:gate and eval:rhythm paths, and emits deterministic per-cell results (no wall-clock, so reruns give identical verdicts).

Commit scorecard.json (target, measured, pass, spread) as a ratchet baseline; a vitest check fails if any previously passing cell drops (AC12), extending the it.fails pattern in scripts/ground-truth/alignment.test.ts.
Tap the six missing .beats.json (beatless as explicit no-beat truth) so every cell exists.
Keep a small live debug:viz and debug:repeat pass only as a confirmation for AC7, AC8 and AC11, run once per slice instead of as the tuning loop.

Defer or split AC5 (onset F on no-kick-124 bass, bassline-kick-120 kick), AC9 (dotted tempo) and AC10 (private cube bars, bass-ink, trio sheets) into separate measured follow-ups; they are not hub regressions.

options.summary: Hybrid of O3 and O2: an offline, deterministic scorecard (hub plus gate plus tracker replayed over every .debug-in WAV) as the tuning loop and ratchet, a thin live wrapper over debug:viz and debug:repeat only for browser-only metrics, a measured cause for every failing cell before any fix, then an additive absolute-scale hub band channel, an onset retune, tempo follow-ups and migration of the private analysis paths, each slice re-scored with no cell allowed to drop.
approach: Tap .beats.json for the six tracks that lack one (beatless gets an explicit no-beat truth) so every cell exists (from O1/O2)

Offline scorecard: decode each WAV and drive the real hub, bassGate, cube trigger and RhythmTracker code headlessly on track time, reusing eval:rhythm --alignment, sweep:onsets and replay:gate paths; write scorecard.json and a markdown table (from O3)
Live wrapper: run debug:viz and debug:repeat 4 times per real track only for clip spread, lock spread, reaction latency and order independence; median-of-4 with a per-metric tolerance (from O2)
Ratchet: a committed baseline plus scorecard:check that fails if any baseline-passing cell fails; every fix slice runs it before merge (O2 and O3)

Cause isolation first: replay the gate and cube trigger on raw BassPulse-scale versus hub normalized bass over the recorded and offline inputs and record which cells each cause explains, in a findings doc, before code changes
Additive hub change: absolute-scale band channel next to the normalized one; dancer gate and cubes threshold read it so pre-hub thresholds keep their meaning

Separate measured slices for onset F (per-band detector retune with sweep:onsets grids), tempo (syncopation-no-kick wrong lock, dotted 100 to 150 follow), and AC10 migration of cubes bars, bass-ink and trio sheets onto hub bands and hub.onsets, finishing with an order-independence check and an all-green scorecard (from O2)

decision_rationale: O4 is the top scorer and the only option besides O2 that covers every AC, which D4 requires. It keeps O3's deterministic offline loop, so tuning one track cannot silently break another, and it uses O2's breadth for the onset, tempo, migration and order-independence work. Unlike O1 it does not retune thresholds against a moving normalized scale, and unlike O2 it does not make slow, noisy live runs the tuning loop.

design.overview: Measure first, then fix, one change at a time. S1 completes ground truth. S2 builds the offline scorecard (tracker, onsets, and gate via stepBassGate on hub frames) and the ratchet, with an applicability matrix. S3 adds the live wrapper, a DEV-only raw BassPulse column next to hub bass, the pre-hub reference column from a worktree, the committed baseline and a findings doc giving each failing cell a measured cause and an owning slice; the user then confirms stretch targets, which slices proceed and any deferrals. Fix slices are serialized (S4 gate input, S5 gate rule, S6 onsets, S7 tempo, S8 clip phase, S9 migration), each regenerating and committing the baseline at merge so AC12 compares against the latest merged baseline. S10 adds order independence and closes with every floor met and stretch results reported.

contracts.name: hub gate-input bass
contracts.definition: Provisional until the S3 ablation. Hub snapshot gains gateBass: { sub, kick, lowEnd }, a read-only field for threshold consumers (dancer gate, cubes trigger, later bass-ink) whose feature is the one the ablation shows restores gate and hit-share cells: a fixed-scale band, a different smoothing, or lower latency. Written in place each frame with no allocation; existing normalized fields and their semantics unchanged

contracts.definition: scorecard.json is an array of { metric, track, visualizer, class, applicable, floor, stretch, prehub, value, spread, runs, source: offline or live, blocking, pass }, plus a header with targets version and the SHA-256 of each .beats.json; n/a cells have applicable false; missing tracks have value null and pass false with status unavailable

contracts.name: scorecard commands
contracts.definition: npm run scorecard (offline, all WAVs), npm run scorecard:live -- --viz NAME (live cells, 4 runs), npm run scorecard:check (exit 1 listing cells when a blocking cell that passed at the latest baseline fails, when a live median worsens beyond the recorded spread, or when a .beats.json hash differs from the baseline)

design.data: Telemetry and raw runs stay in git-ignored .debug-out; .debug-in audio and tapped .beats.json stay local and uncommitted, so the real-track ratchet is a local discipline run before each merge; CI covers only the synthetic ratchet test. Committed: scorecard.json summary, baseline with sidecar hashes, findings doc.
design.ux: No UI change except restored reactions: the dancer gate engages sooner, cubes fire on more beats. Developer UX: one command gives the full pass or fail table.
design.accessibility: No UI surface changes; existing e2e axe checks stay green.
design.security_privacy: Client-side only; no new network calls; audio files are not committed.
design.observability: Scorecard table and baseline diff per slice; existing DEV telemetry columns plus the abs bands added to debug:viz output.
design.rollout: One PR per slice, serialized, with Conventional Commit titles (S1 to S3 as test or chore except S3's DEV-only telemetry column as chore, fixes as fix). Each fix PR attaches scorecard:check output and its live cells, and commits the regenerated baseline. C1 is additive, so each consumer switch is revertible by reverting its PR; Cloudflare rollback covers production. Visual baselines regenerated in S9 are accepted only with a measured reaction cell that did not drop.

test_strategy.unit: Specs beside each new module: scorecard aggregation, targets, ratchet compare, hub abs channel scaling and no-allocation, gate on abs input; keep 95 percent coverage
test_strategy.integration: Offline scorecard over the synthetic tracks runs in vitest as a ratchet test like scripts/ground-truth/alignment.test.ts; real tracks run locally since .debug-in is not committed
test_strategy.e2e: npm run test:e2e after build for every rendering slice; S8 adds an order-independence spec that opens two hub-fed visualizers in both orders
test_strategy.manual: npm run dev with each real track on each hub-fed visualizer plus cubes and trio-color-wave after S4, S7 and at the end; watch the dancer and cubes, because numbers cannot show whether it looks right
test_strategy.non_functional: Bundle within .size-limit.json and Lighthouse budget; no per-frame allocation in the hub change; offline scorecard full run under 10 minutes

open_questions.question: Does the offline replay match live telemetry closely enough to be the tuning loop, and at what tolerance?
Which fix slices proceed after the S3 findings review?
Are the stretch numbers (90 percent hit share, 10 percent false fires, 2 s gate, 30 ms plus a frame) right once the pre-hub column is in?

findings.finding: C1 and S4 freeze an absolute band channel 'calibrated to BassPulse raw RMS (120 Hz low-pass)' before the cause is measured. Hub bands are the mean of log(1 + 30 * magnitude) frame energy divided by a running peak (audioHub.ts:177-185, hubConfig.ts:17), a different feature from BassPulse's filtered raw RMS, so a fixed gain cannot make the scales match. bassGateConfig.ts also learns the kick phase from BassPulse lag (0.11-0.21 beats) and its thresholds are rise-relative (BASS_GATE_ONSET_RISE 0.08), so smoothing, latency and log compression are as likely a cause as scale (K2). The scale cause is only an inference (brief line 34). gate-replay (gateReplay.ts) replays recorded columns, which hold hub low end only, so hub-era telemetry cannot be replayed on raw BassPulse and 'replay raw vs hub' has no recorded raw input.
findings.suggestion: Mark C1 provisional until S3 findings. In S3, record raw BassPulse alongside hub bass in debug:viz and replay both through stepBassGate. Create S4's contract only for the cause that the ablation shows, with abs possibly replaced by a smoothing or latency fix.
findings.resolution: Changed: C1 is now a provisional gateBass field whose feature (scale, smoothing or latency) the S3 ablation picks; S3 adds a DEV-only raw BassPulse column so both inputs can be replayed through stepBassGate.

findings.finding: AC2 and AC5 cannot be met as written. onset-sweep scores per-band F only against synthetic ground-truth tracks that carry labelled onsets (onsetSweepRunner.ts:23-33); tapped .beats.json tracks get only onset rates and alignment lift (onset-sweep.ts:93-94). The no-kick-124 and bassline-kick-120 failures are synthetic tracks, not .debug-in files. So AC2's 'appears in every scorecard metric' fails for the six tapped tracks, and beatless has no beat error (AC4) or reaction share (AC8). AC3 (2 percent bpm vs sidecar) is also ill-defined for drifting-tempo and 6-8-time, where a single sidecar bpm is not truth.
findings.suggestion: Give the scorecard an explicit applicability matrix (metric x track class: synthetic, tapped, beatless, drifting) with 'n/a' cells that do not count toward the 100 percent. Define drifting-tempo AC3 as per-segment or local bpm, and AC5 as synthetic-only. Amend AC2 to match.
findings.resolution: Changed: added an applicability matrix (D14, C2 class and applicable fields); AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 amended; drifting-tempo uses local bpm per 8-beat window; onset F only on labelled tracks.

findings.finding: Several target cells have no owning slice. AC6 for lonley (8.0 s) and syncopationbass (16.8-17.9 s) are gate-rule behavior that predates the hub, but S4's draft_paths are hub, dancing-character and cubes, and exclude app/features/rhythm/bassGate*.ts. AC7 (clip spread 0.199-0.53, lock spread) was measured before rhythm S6 and is a re-select phase problem, not a hub-bass one, yet only S3 (measure) and S4 (bass abs) reference it. Goal 'every cell to its target' and D4 therefore have uncovered cells, while the plan counts only 'covers_all_acs'.
findings.suggestion: After S3, add a per-cell owner column in hub-scorecard.md. Add a gate-rule slice (bassGate.ts) for AC6 stragglers and a clip-phase slice for AC7, or mark those cells as pre-existing non-hub failures needing a user decision.
findings.resolution: Changed: added S5 gate-rule slice for lonley and syncopationbass and S8 clip-phase slice for AC7; findings doc assigns an owning slice per cell; deferral rule D11.

findings.finding: AC6 and AC8 are defined relative to 'pre-hub' values (0.3 s, 3.5 s, 30 of 61, 'latency no worse than pre-hub'), but D1 measures only the current branch, and the pre-hub figures come from older docs, measured under different harness and tolerance. Pre-hub reaction latency is not recorded anywhere in the plan. The '30 of 61' is a threshold-crossing count (presentation-audit.md:66-78) while AC8 says 'reaction fires on beats', so metric definitions differ. The regression targets are therefore unmeasurable and may be unreachable.
findings.suggestion: In S3, check out the pre-hub commit (b449f56^ or 5131f35^) in a worktree and run the same scorecard to add a 'pre-hub reference' column. Define the crossing metric once in targets.ts and use it in AC8 and success_metrics.
findings.resolution: Changed: S3 runs the same scorecard on the pre-hub commit as a reference column (D8); hit share defined once in targets.ts and used in AC8 and the metrics; stretch targets above pre-hub (D9, D10).

findings.finding: The ratchet and AC1/AC12 assume deterministic verdicts, but live cells (clip spread p95, lock spread, reaction latency, AC11) come from a browser with 4 runs and a 'tolerance band'. A cell near its target flips between reruns, which would break 'rerunning gives the same pass or fail' (AC1) and make 'zero cells that pass at baseline fail' (success metric, D4) flap or mask real drops (K1 admits the masking). With a p95 over 4 runs the statistic is just the worst or second-worst sample.
findings.suggestion: Make only offline, deterministic cells blocking in scorecard:check. Treat live cells as advisory with a stated rule (for example, pass if at least 3 of 4 runs pass, regression only when the median worsens beyond a measured run-to-run spread recorded in S3). Replace the p95 target with a statistic that is meaningful at n=4.
findings.resolution: Changed: only offline cells block; live cells pass at 3 of 4 runs and regress only beyond the S3 spread (D13); AC7 replaced p95 with a 3-of-4 rule.

findings.finding: Slice ordering leaves interacting changes parallel. S4, S5 and S6 all depend only on S3 but couple: S5 retunes hub onsets and rhythmConfig, which feed the tracker (S6) and the gate's tempoLocked input (S4, AC6). Rebaselining after each merge is undefined: AC12 says 'passed before the slice' but the committed baseline is made once in S3, so S6 may be measured against a baseline that S4 and S5 have already moved. S4 and S5 both edit app/features/audio/hub/.
findings.suggestion: Serialize S4 -> S5 -> S6 (or S5 before S4's gate checks) and require the baseline to be regenerated, reviewed and committed at each merge. State that AC12 compares against the latest merged baseline.
findings.resolution: Changed: fix slices serialized S4 to S9; baseline regenerated and committed at each merge; AC12 compares against the latest merged baseline.

findings.finding: S2 is sized M and called a 'headless deterministic replay of hub, gate, cube trigger and tracker', but the cube trigger and dancer bass path live in React hooks and three.js scene code (useCubesScene.ts:91-151, useDancingCharacterScene.ts:283-288, dancingCharacterScene.ts:396). Running them in node requires extracting logic or duplicating it, which risks the offline replay testing a copy (K1) and touches production code in a slice marked R1. The 'under 10 minutes' offline budget is unverified. The plan's own gaps (AC5, AC9 need tracker offline replays too) make it larger than M.
findings.suggestion: Make S2 scope explicit: list which cells are offline (tracker, onsets, gate via stepBassGate on hub frames) and which stay live (cube trigger, render). Raise S2 to L or split it into a tracker/onset/gate scorecard and a later cube-trigger extraction that sits in the S4 refactor. Raise risk to R2 if app code moves.
findings.resolution: Changed: S2 scope lists offline cells (tracker, onsets, gate on hub frames) and is now L; cube-trigger extraction moved into S4 (R2).

findings.finding: S7 (AC10 migration of cubes bars, bass-ink and trio sheets) is not a regression fix and conflicts with the 'no visual redesign' non-goal and D4. bass-ink currently reads raw BassPulse (useBassInkScene.ts:183,218); moving it onto the peak-normalized hub bands could create the same class of regression the plan is chasing. K5 mitigates by 'visual baselines regenerated and reviewed', which turns the e2e visual regression guard into an approval step. There is no pre-hub reaction cell for bass-ink and trio, so AC12 has nothing to protect them.
findings.suggestion: Move S7 out of the regression plan or gate it on a measured reaction cell for each target visualizer before and after. Migrate bass-ink onto C1 abs bands only after S4 proves them, and do not accept regenerated visual baselines unless the diff is within an agreed tolerance.
findings.resolution: Changed: S9 measures a reaction cell per visualizer before moving it, bass-ink moves only onto the proven gateBass, and visual baselines are accepted only with no cell drop (D12).

findings.finding: AC9 depends on 'the time set by rhythm-stability-followups AC6' and Q3 leaves that value as a non-blocking open question, though it is in a repo doc. The finding that the dotted 100 to 150 change 'never followed in 30 s' (findings:489-491) means S6 is probably tracker architecture work, which the non-goals forbid beyond a 'measured cause'. AC9 is untestable as written and S6 may be infeasible without breaking D4 (K3).
findings.suggestion: Resolve Q3 before approval and write the number into AC9. State a deferral rule: if S6 needs a tracker redesign, AC9 and the syncopation-no-kick lock become a separate plan and the 100 percent goal excludes them with user sign-off.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC9 rewritten from rhythm-stability-followups AC6 (no time limit, boundary rule, 0.00 false changes) with an explicit deferral rule; Q3 removed.

findings.finding: The ratchet depends on local, uncommitted data: .debug-in audio and Trevor's tapped .beats.json are not committed, so the committed baseline cannot be reproduced by CI or by anyone else, and scorecard:check behavior with missing tracks is unspecified (skip, fail or pass). Tap truth is operator-specific, so the baseline moves if the six sidecars are re-tapped (K4 even suggests taps are redone). The synthetic vitest ratchet only covers synthetic tracks. The goal 'make the scorecard a re-runnable no-regression check for later hub work' is therefore only locally true.
findings.suggestion: Specify missing-track behavior (report 'unavailable', never 'pass'), store a hash of each .beats.json and the target-version in the baseline, and fail the check on sidecar hash change unless the baseline is regenerated. Say plainly in the plan that the real-track ratchet is a local discipline.
findings.resolution: Changed: C2 header stores .beats.json hashes and targets version; missing tracks show unavailable and never pass; design.data says the real-track ratchet is local (K8).
